title: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us
body:
Read the chapter → [Judges 6](/bible/judges/6)

**[Judges 6:1-2](/bible/judges/6#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/judges/6#v1)</sup> And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/judges/6#v2)</sup> And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel: and because of the Midianites the children of Israel made them the dens which are in the mountains, and caves, and strong holds.

- Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years. That is our manner: the Most High delivers us, we get a little bit of freedom, and we go right back to wickedness. The same thing goes on today; we get relaxed, and the Lord has to remind us, putting us right back into hard bondage, that this is not our rest.
- Because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made them the dens in the mountains, and caves, and strongholds; Israel hid in the mountains of their own land.

**[Judges 6:3-6](/bible/judges/6#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/judges/6#v3)</sup> And so it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east, even they came up against them;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/judges/6#v4)</sup> And they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, till thou come unto Gaza, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/judges/6#v5)</sup> For they came up with their cattle and their tents, and they came as grasshoppers for multitude; for both they and their camels were without number: and they entered into the land to destroy it.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/judges/6#v6)</sup> And Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites; and the children of Israel cried unto the Lord.

- When Israel had sown, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up as grasshoppers for multitude, destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished. That goes right into the curses.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:21-22](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v21)</sup> The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee, until he have consumed thee from off the land, whither thou goest to possess it.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v22)</sup> The Lord shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.

    The Lord shall smite thee with blasting and with mildew; the blasting and the mildew go into famine, exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops.

**[Judges 6:7-10](/bible/judges/6#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/judges/6#v7)</sup> And it came to pass, when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord because of the Midianites,
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/judges/6#v8)</sup> That the Lord sent a prophet unto the children of Israel, which said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you forth out of the house of bondage;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/judges/6#v9)</sup> And I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all that oppressed you, and drave them out from before you, and gave you their land;
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/judges/6#v10)</sup> And I said unto you, I am the Lord your God; fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but ye have not obeyed my voice.

- When Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent a prophet to remind them: I brought you up from Egypt out of the house of bondage, and I said, fear not the gods of the Amorites in whose land ye dwell, but ye have not obeyed my voice. The judgment came with a reason attached.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 10:15-16](/bible/genesis/10#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/10#v15)</sup> And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/10#v16)</sup> And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite,

    The Amorites go back into the Hamites: the lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan.

**[Judges 6:11-12](/bible/judges/6#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/judges/6#v11)</sup> And there came an angel of the Lord, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abi–ezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/judges/6#v12)</sup> And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him, and said unto him, The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.

- An angel of the Lord came and sat under an oak in Ophrah, while Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites; that is how hard the oppression sat on the land, that a man hid his own harvest to keep it.
- The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 1:7](/bible/hebrews/1#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/hebrews/1#v7)</sup> And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.

    The angels are spirits and ministers made of the flame of fire that sits under the throne of heaven; they go and come as they please, change forms, vanish into thin air, and one of them can slay an hundred fourscore and five thousand men in a single night.
  - **[Hebrews 13:1-2](/bible/hebrews/13#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/hebrews/13#v1)</sup> Let brotherly love continue.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/hebrews/13#v2)</sup> Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

    Be not forgetful to entertain strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares, just as Tobias in the book of Tobit entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself.

**[Judges 6:13](/bible/judges/6#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/judges/6#v13)</sup> And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt? but now the Lord hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites.

- Gideon answers, oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us, and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? A lot of us ask that same question today when we watch our people judged in the streets over and over: if we be the chosen people, why does all of this happen to us?

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 12:6-8](/bible/hebrews/12#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/hebrews/12#v6)</sup> For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/hebrews/12#v7)</sup> If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/hebrews/12#v8)</sup> But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

    Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth; if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards and not sons. That is why the other nations never suffer the judgments we suffer: the chastening of the Most High does not pertain to them, but he chastens us because we are his sons.
  - **[Hebrews 12:9-11](/bible/hebrews/12#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/hebrews/12#v9)</sup> Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hebrews/12#v10)</sup> For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/hebrews/12#v11)</sup> Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.

    No chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous but grievous, and it does look grievous to all of us; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness, which is the kingdom, eternal life, and everlasting peace for them which are exercised thereby.

- Gideon says the Lord hath forsaken us, and that is the same thought our people carry today when you hit the streets teaching. But God has not forsaken us; it is actually we that have forsaken God.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 2:31](/bible/jeremiah/2#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/jeremiah/2#v31)</sup> O generation, see ye the word of the Lord. Have I been a wilderness unto Israel? a land of darkness? wherefore say my people, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee?

    Have I been a wilderness unto Israel, a land of darkness? The Lord asks, am I not able to be found, am I not right in front of you? Yet my people say, We are lords; we will come no more unto thee.
  - **[Jeremiah 2:13](/bible/jeremiah/2#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/jeremiah/2#v13)</sup> For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.

    My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns that can hold no water. The water is the word, and the broken cisterns are the religions we hewed out for ourselves, Christianity, Islam, and now politics, the newest religion our people put their faith in.

**[Judges 6:14-15](/bible/judges/6#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/judges/6#v14)</sup> And the Lord looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/judges/6#v15)</sup> And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.

- The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Corinthians 1:26-28](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v26)</sup> For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called:
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v27)</sup> But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v28)</sup> And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are:

    Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called; God hath chosen the foolish, the weak, the base, and the despised things of the world to confound the mighty.
  - **[James 2:5](/bible/james/2#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/james/2#v5)</sup> Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

    Hath not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him? The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him.

- Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

  Precepts:
  - **[Luke 16:15](/bible/luke/16#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/luke/16#v15)</sup> And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

    Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God; you could be president, a general, the highest grossing rapper, or the leading scorer in the league, and none of it matters to the Lord.
  - **[Isaiah 49:5](/bible/isaiah/49#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/isaiah/49#v5)</sup> And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.

    The servant formed from the womb to bring Jacob again to the Lord is glorious in the eyes of the Lord; gathering Israel back is the highest honor on earth.
  - **[1 Samuel 16:6-7](/bible/1-samuel/16#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/16#v6)</sup> And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the Lord’s anointed is before him.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/16#v7)</sup> But the Lord said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.

    Samuel looked on Eliab and thought, surely the Lord's anointed is before him, but the Lord said, look not on his countenance or the height of his stature; man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart. You short brothers can be great leaders.

**[Judges 6:16-18](/bible/judges/6#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/judges/6#v16)</sup> And the Lord said unto him, Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/judges/6#v17)</sup> And he said unto him, If now I have found grace in thy sight, then shew me a sign that thou talkest with me.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/judges/6#v18)</sup> Depart not hence, I pray thee, until I come unto thee, and bring forth my present, and set it before thee. And he said, I will tarry until thou come again.

- The Lord promises, surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man. Gideon asks for a sign that it is really the Lord talking with him; the least in his father's house wanted to be sure he was not talking to himself.

**[Judges 6:19-21](/bible/judges/6#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/judges/6#v19)</sup> And Gideon went in, and made ready a kid, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of flour: the flesh he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out unto him under the oak, and presented it.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/judges/6#v20)</sup> And the angel of God said unto him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/judges/6#v21)</sup> Then the angel of the Lord put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the Lord departed out of his sight.

- Gideon brings a kid and unleavened cakes, and the angel touches the flesh and the cakes with the end of his staff; fire rises up out of the rock and consumes them, and the angel departs out of his sight, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Corinthians 15:40](/bible/1-corinthians/15#v40)**
    > <sup>[40](/bible/1-corinthians/15#v40)</sup> There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.

    There are celestial bodies and bodies terrestrial; our earthly bodies are made of the ground, but the angels have celestial bodies, which is why they can appear, disappear, and stand all around us right now listening and recording without us knowing.
  - **[Matthew 18:10](/bible/matthew/18#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/matthew/18#v10)</sup> Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.

    Christ said of the little ones that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of his Father; every one of us that has repented has a guardian angel assigned to minister to us and nudge us in the way the Lord wants our life to go.

**[Judges 6:22-24](/bible/judges/6#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/judges/6#v22)</sup> And when Gideon perceived that he was an angel of the Lord, Gideon said, Alas, O Lord God! for because I have seen an angel of the Lord face to face.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/judges/6#v23)</sup> And the Lord said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/judges/6#v24)</sup> Then Gideon built an altar there unto the Lord, and called it Jehovah–shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi–ezrites.

- When Gideon perceived he had seen an angel of the Lord face to face, he feared death, but the Lord said, peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die. Gideon built an altar there and called it Jehovah-shalom, which is, the Lord is peace.

**[Judges 6:25-27](/bible/judges/6#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/judges/6#v25)</sup> And it came to pass the same night, that the Lord said unto him, Take thy father’s young bullock, even the second bullock of seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the grove that is by it:
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/judges/6#v26)</sup> And build an altar unto the Lord thy God upon the top of this rock, in the ordered place, and take the second bullock, and offer a burnt sacrifice with the wood of the grove which thou shalt cut down.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/judges/6#v27)</sup> Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as the Lord had said unto him: and so it was, because he feared his father’s household, and the men of the city, that he could not do it by day, that he did it by night.

- The same night the Lord tells him to throw down his own father's altar of Baal, cut down the grove by it, and build an altar unto the Lord in its place. Notice this: even before the split of the kingdom, the tribes that would become the northern kingdom were already dabbling with Baal, worshipping the Lord in some fashion while holding onto the idol.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Kings 12:28](/bible/1-kings/12#v28)**
    > <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/12#v28)</sup> Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

    That is why it was such an easy transition when Jeroboam set up the golden calves and said, behold thy gods, O Israel; the north had been dealing with Baal long before the split ever happened.

- Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord said, but by night, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city; they worshipped that idol and would have killed him in the daylight.

**[Judges 6:28-32](/bible/judges/6#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/judges/6#v28)</sup> And when the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was cast down, and the grove was cut down that was by it, and the second bullock was offered upon the altar that was built.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/judges/6#v29)</sup> And they said one to another, Who hath done this thing? And when they enquired and asked, they said, Gideon the son of Joash hath done this thing.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/judges/6#v30)</sup> Then the men of the city said unto Joash, Bring out thy son, that he may die: because he hath cast down the altar of Baal, and because he hath cut down the grove that was by it.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/judges/6#v31)</sup> And Joash said unto all that stood against him, Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him? he that will plead for him, let him be put to death whilst it is yet morning: if he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/judges/6#v32)</sup> Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal plead against him, because he hath thrown down his altar.

- In the morning the men of the city found the altar of Baal cast down, and when they inquired, they said, Gideon the son of Joash hath done this thing. He crept at night, but somebody was peeping out a window; he was doing the right thing and still got told on.
- The grove they worshipped was a carved tree stump, cut and shaped to look like a particular god; that is the idol Gideon cut down.
- The men demand his death, but Joash stands up for his son: will ye plead for Baal? If he be a god, let him plead for himself, because one hath cast down his altar. Obviously he is no god; he is an idol. So that day Gideon was named Jerubbaal, saying, let Baal plead against him.

**[Judges 6:33-35](/bible/judges/6#v33)**

> <sup>[33](/bible/judges/6#v33)</sup> Then all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the children of the east were gathered together, and went over, and pitched in the valley of Jezreel.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/judges/6#v34)</sup> But the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet; and Abi–ezer was gathered after him.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/judges/6#v35)</sup> And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh; who also was gathered after him: and he sent messengers unto Asher, and unto Zebulun, and unto Naphtali; and they came up to meet them.

- The Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east gathered and pitched in the valley of Jezreel, but the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon; he blew a trumpet, and Abiezer, Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali came up to meet him.
- Those tribes are warriors; do not get it twisted. You see how Zebulun and Naphtali, who are in the south Americas right now, get down: that warrior spirit is still in them, only right now it has turned on each other, and the Most High is going to correct it and turn it right again.

**[Judges 6:36-40](/bible/judges/6#v36)**

> <sup>[36](/bible/judges/6#v36)</sup> And Gideon said unto God, If thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said,
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/judges/6#v37)</sup> Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/judges/6#v38)</sup> And it was so: for he rose up early on the morrow, and thrust the fleece together, and wringed the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/judges/6#v39)</sup> And Gideon said unto God, Let not thine anger be hot against me, and I will speak but this once: let me prove, I pray thee, but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/judges/6#v40)</sup> And God did so that night: for it was dry upon the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground.

- Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 17:8](/bible/numbers/17#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/numbers/17#v8)</sup> And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.

    The same power made Aaron's rod bud, bloom blossoms, and yield almonds overnight.
  - **[2 Kings 20:11](/bible/2-kings/20#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/20#v11)</sup> And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.

    For Hezekiah he brought the shadow ten degrees backward on the sundial; time itself obeys him.
  - **[Matthew 12:39](/bible/matthew/12#v39)**
    > <sup>[39](/bible/matthew/12#v39)</sup> But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:

    But do not ask for signs like that anymore; an evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign. He gave us all the signs back in the day, he split the Red Sea and we still became rebellious, so the walk we are in now is by faith.
